# QC (Acceptance Criteria) Audit Patterns

**Source:** 16 initiatives from scripps-mcp/SRD corpus, June 2026 (EDMV2 seed).
**Note:** QC findings are generated by `edm-qc-auditor` after each implementation wave. This document will grow richer as EDMV2 and subsequent initiatives complete Phase 6.
**Auto-updated** by orchestrator after each QC audit round (EDMV2-80a).

---

## Top Recurring Findings

Frequency: [x/16] = appeared in x of 16 audited initiatives (many pre-EDMV2 initiatives lacked formal QC; counts are approximate).

| # | Pattern | Frequency | Typical severity |
|---|---------|-----------|-----------------|
| 1 | AC verified by code inspection only — no runnable assertion | ~8/16 | P1 |
| 2 | AC passes but neighboring regression introduced | ~6/16 | P0 |
| 3 | PARTIAL verdict left unresolved at phase close | ~5/16 | P1 |
| 4 | QC artifact written to wrong location / not committed | ~4/16 | P1 |
| 5 | Implementer modifies test to achieve AC pass (TDD violation) | ~3/16 | P0 |

### 1. AC verified by inspection only (8/16)
- QC auditor marks AC PASS because the code looks correct, but no automated test runs the AC end-to-end
- "Code review will verify" as a substitute for a runnable assertion

### 2. Regressions in neighboring code (6/16)
- The ticket's own ACs all pass but an adjacent feature's tests now fail
- Implementer changed a shared utility without updating all callers

### 3. Unresolved PARTIAL verdicts (5/16)
- QC auditor assigns PARTIAL ("needs running service to verify") but the ticket is closed without ever reaching a PASS or explicit runtime-deferred decision
- PARTIAL verdicts pile up and are never adjudicated

### 4. QC artifact in wrong location (4/16)
- `qc-auditor` writes its report to a temp path or the wrong PREFIX directory; it's not committed and not findable at phase review

### 5. Test retrofitted to match code (3/16)
- In TDD mode: implementer could not satisfy the original test, so modified the test assertion to match what the code actually does
- Defeats the specification value of the test

---

## Anti-Patterns

### PASS based on code structure, not behavior
QC marks PASS because the function signature looks right — it never verifies the function is actually called or produces correct output.
**Fix:** Every PASS verdict cites a test command and output snippet, not code structure.

### Closing tickets with PARTIAL verdicts
PARTIAL means "cannot verify statically; requires runtime." If the initiative closes with unresolved PARTIAL verdicts, nobody knows if those ACs ever passed.
**Fix:** Before phase close, every PARTIAL must be either (a) verified at runtime and upgraded to PASS, or (b) explicitly documented in the exec-report as a known runtime dependency.

### QC report not committed
The QC artifact is written during the phase but not staged and committed. Reviewers can't see the QC verdict history in the PR.
**Fix:** The orchestrator stages and commits `qc/` artifacts at the end of each implementation wave (EDMV2-107 per-gate commit pattern).

### Implementer self-QC
The same agent that implemented the ticket also performs QC. The agent's own framing of the requirements biases the verdict.
**Fix:** `edm-qc-auditor` is always a separate agent from `edm-implementer`. Never reuse the implementer's context for QC.

---

## Pre-Flight Checklist

Run before declaring a ticket's QC complete:

- [ ] **Every AC has a runnable test command cited** in the QC report — not just "inspected code."
- [ ] **Regression check:** The full test suite (not just the ticket's tests) passes. Any new failures in unrelated tests are flagged as regressions before closing the ticket.
- [ ] **PARTIAL verdicts adjudicated:** Any AC marked PARTIAL has either been verified at runtime (upgraded to PASS) or explicitly documented in the exec-report with a rationale for deferral.
- [ ] **QC artifact committed:** The `qc/{ticket-id}.md` report is staged and committed to the initiative branch.
- [ ] **TDD compliance (if applicable):** In TDD mode, the QC report includes a TDD compliance pass showing each test predates its implementation and was not modified after implementation began.

---

## What a Passing QC Round Looks Like

- **Every AC verdict (PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL) cites evidence:** a test command + output snippet for PASS; a rationale and runtime-deferred note for PARTIAL; a reproduction path for FAIL.
- **No regressions:** the test suite passes at the same rate as before the wave.
- **PARTIAL verdicts are documented** in the exec-report with explicit "will verify at runtime by [condition]" language — they don't disappear silently.
- **QC artifact is committed** on the initiative branch alongside the implementation artifacts.
- **TDD compliance verified** (TDD mode only): for each ticket, test file timestamps precede implementation file timestamps and test assertions were not weakened post-implementation.
